agent_summary: NETs (cfDNA, nucleosomes, MPO-DNA, CitH3) and circulating extracellular histones are grade-3 human severity mechanisms in malaria and sepsis, have canine assays already used in sepsis, IMHA, heatstroke and pancreatitis, and have never been measured in dogs with babesiosis: both are clear gaps. The granule-protein seed row is only partly filled in dogs: MPXI is an intracellular analyser index and NGAL studies are renal, so released plasma MPO/elastase and calprotectin/S100A12 are split out as added rows and are also gaps. DS07 (CB112 serum proteome, severity-labelled) already carries master proteins for histone H4, S100A8 and lactotransferrin, of which only lactotransferrin was reported.

mechanisms.mechanism: Neutrophil extracellular traps (cell-free DNA, MPO-DNA, citrullinated histone H3)
mechanisms.human_direction: higher in severe or fatal disease: cfDNA rises from uncomplicated to cerebral malaria and separates fatal retinopathy-positive cases; NET counts, elastase and CitH3 rise with severity in falciparum and knowlesi malaria; sepsis meta-analyses report higher cfDNA in non-survivors. Counterpoint: in HU008 (341 ICU patients) cfDNA and MPO-DNA did not predict death after severity adjustment; only an ex vivo NET-induction assay did.

CB028: review, NETs only as a hypothesis for thrombocytopenia
CB141: NETosis cited from literature, not measured
CB145: thromboinflammation cohort CH03, NETs discussed only
CB098: keyword hit only, no NET marker measured

mechanisms.testable_detail: DS06 has PADI4 (ENSCAFG00000015768), whole-blood gene expression only, a NET-capacity proxy rather than circulating NETs. No DS07 master protein, no DS02 variable. Circulating cfDNA or nucleosomes would need stored plasma; sample type changes cfDNA values.
mechanisms.notes: Canine cfDNA fluorometry is linear and repeatable and is prognostic in canine sepsis (cfDNA per neutrophil higher in non-survivors, https://doi.org/10.1111/vec.12773); nucleosome ELISA (Nu.Q H3.1) and a histone-DNA ELISA have been evaluated in dogs. Haemolysis and icterus interfere with the nucleosome ELISA (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.vetimm.2015.10.014), a real limitation in haemolytic babesiosis. A dog cfDNA sequencing study (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ygeno.2018.05.020) detected Babesia DNA, not host NETs.

mechanisms.human_direction: higher with severity and death: in paediatric cerebral malaria circulating histones are raised, roughly half of parasite origin, and track brain swelling; in 420 ICU patients histone levels correlate with organ injury markers and SOFA; in two smaller sepsis cohorts histones are far higher in non-survivors
cb_rejected: CB010: parasite side only. A B. canis secreted histone was found in the parasite secretome from cultured infected RBC, not measured in dog plasma and not by severity
CB107: review, histones named as NET components
CB145: histones named in the thromboinflammation narrative, not measured

mechanisms.testable_detail: DS07 master L7N0L3 Histone H4 (H4C7, 11 percent coverage), plus three master_candidate H4 entries (Q6B829, J9NRV0, F2Z4N2). DS07 rows carry the CB112 complicated/uncomplicated/control labels, so a severity contrast of serum histone H4 abundance is possible from the public file; abundance in a TMT serum proteome is not a validated histone concentration. No DS06 gene in the counts file, no DS02 variable.
mechanisms.notes: Serum histones have been measured in dogs by ELISA in heatstroke (associated with severity) and in acute pancreatitis, and nucleosome assays in canine cancer, so a canine method exists. Parasite-derived histones are plausible in Babesia (CB010 secretome) but untested in dog blood, and host versus parasite origin would need species-distinguishing peptides, as in the human cerebral malaria work.

mechanisms.mechanism: Neutrophil granule proteins (MPO, elastase, lactoferrin, NGAL, S100A8/A9)
mechanisms.human_direction: higher in severe disease: plasma elastase, MPO and proteinase 3 raised in retinopathy-positive cerebral malaria (lactoferrin and lipocalin were not), neutrophil granule transcripts raised in sepsis non-survivors and in all severe malaria phenotypes in dual RNA-seq, NGAL predicts malarial acute kidney injury

cb_confirmed.what: neutrophil myeloperoxidase index (MPXI, ADVIA 2120) in 140 infected dogs vs 20 controls, compared between non-survivors and survivors (median 22.8 vs 19.0, not significant) and correlated with cytokines; MPXI is intracellular MPO content, not released plasma MPO

serum proteome of 32 B. rossi cases (18 uncomplicated, 14 complicated) and 20 controls; lactotransferrin reported for the first time in this disease and validated by western blot (control vs complicated P = 0.003); S100A8 present among DS07 master proteins but not reported
urinary and plasma NGAL at presentation in 35 B. rossi cases (complicated vs uncomplicated) and 10 controls; both NGAL measures did not differ by complication status
serum and urine TMT proteomics in 22 B. canis cases stratified by renal dysfunction; urinary NGAL proposed as an early renal marker
urinary NGAL and KIM-1 across IRIS AKI grades in dogs with babesiosis or leptospirosis

mechanisms.testable_detail: DS07 masters F1PR54 lactotransferrin (6 percent) and C0LQL0 Protein S100 (S100A8, 9 percent), plus master_candidate J9P8S3 S100A8; DS06 has LTF, LCN2, S100A8, S100A12 and CAMP. No DS02 variable.
mechanisms.notes: Counted units: CH03 (CB050), CB112, CB053 and CH06/CB103; CB124 adds a fifth but mixes leptospirosis and reports no babesiosis-only severity contrast, so it is not counted. The row is only nominally covered: NGAL is partly a renal tubular marker rather than a neutrophil activation marker, MPXI is cellular not released, and no study measured plasma MPO, elastase or calprotectin. See the two added rows.

mechanisms.mechanism: Released (plasma) myeloperoxidase and neutrophil elastase, as degranulation markers distinct from the cellular MPXI
mechanisms.human_direction: higher in severe disease: plasma elastase and MPO raised in retinopathy-positive cerebral malaria, soluble elastase rises with severity and with acute lung injury in knowlesi malaria, plasma MPO correlates with cfDNA in fatal paediatric cerebral malaria, neutrophil degranulation genes raised in sepsis non-survivors

mechanisms.testable_detail: No MPO or ELANE master protein in DS07 and neither gene in the DS06 counts; no DS02 variable. A canine neutrophil elastase ELISA exists (purified canine NE, rabbit antibodies), and MPO has been assayed in canine CSF and serum in steroid-responsive meningitis-arteritis, so archived serum or plasma such as DS07's would be needed.
mechanisms.notes: Split from F3-03 because the only canine babesiosis MPO measure (CB050 MPXI) estimates granule content inside neutrophils and would be expected to move opposite to released MPO. The canine NE ELISA has modest spiking recovery (27 to 114 percent), so analytical validation in haemolysed serum would be needed first.

mechanisms.mechanism: Calprotectin (S100A8/A9) and S100A12 as circulating neutrophil activation alarmins
mechanisms.human_direction: higher with severity: a 21-cohort meta-analysis gives a pooled prognostic AUC of about 0.74 for circulating calprotectin in acute infection and sepsis; single cohorts link it to hospital mortality independently of renal function and to sepsis-associated AKI; S100A8/A9 genes sit in the neutrophil granule signature of severe malaria. Effects are moderate and calprotectin did not beat clinical severity scores.
cb_rejected: CB112: S100A8 (C0LQL0, J9P8S3) is present among the DS07 master proteins but calprotectin was not reported or validated in the article
no other CB note or text reports calprotectin, S100A8, S100A9 or S100A12 measurement in babesiosis

mechanisms.testable_detail: DS07 master C0LQL0 Protein S100 (S100A8, 9 percent) and master_candidate J9P8S3 S100A8, in a file with complicated/uncomplicated/control labels, so a severity contrast of serum S100A8 abundance can be run now; DS06 has S100A8 and S100A12 whole-blood expression (transcript, not circulating protein). No DS02 variable. A concentration measurement would need stored serum and the canine radioimmunoassays.
mechanisms.notes: Canine calprotectin and canine S100A12 were purified from dog leukocytes and have analytically validated species-specific radioimmunoassays with reference intervals, so this is among the most readily testable F3 gaps. S100A9 was not detected as a DS07 master protein, so the heterodimer cannot be confirmed from the public file alone.
